questions.question: In the task board, why does `moveTask` have no `invalidatesTags`?
options: The optimistic patch already makes the cache match the server, so a refetch would only add traffic
Tags only work with queries that take arguments
Invalidation would undo the optimistic patch permanently
questions.explanation: On success the patched cache equals the server state; on failure patch.undo() restores it. Refetching the list would be redundant.

questions.question: Moving blocked task 3 to Done returns HTTP 409. What does the board show after `await` of the mutation?
options: Task 3 stays in Done until the page reloads
Task 3 is back in Doing, because the catch block called patch.undo()
The whole task list is refetched and emptied
questions.explanation: onQueryStarted applies the patch immediately; when queryFulfilled rejects, patch.undo() reverts the cached list, so task 3 returns to Doing.

questions.question: Why does `selectAllTasks` return a module-level `EMPTY` array instead of `r.data ?? []`?
options: A new [] on every call would give a new reference while loading and defeat memoisation downstream
Redux state cannot contain empty arrays
TypeScript cannot infer the type of []
RTK Query requires a frozen array
questions.explanation: Memoised selectors compare inputs by reference. A fresh empty array each time would make selectBoardColumns recompute and return a new object on every call.

questions.question: Why did the test call `tasksApi.util.resetApiState()` after unsubscribing?
options: To make the rollback assertion pass
To reset the UI slice's filter
To clear the cache-expiry timer (keepUnusedDataFor) that otherwise kept the process alive for about a minute
questions.explanation: After the last subscriber leaves, RTK Query keeps the entry for keepUnusedDataFor (60 seconds by default) using a timer. Resetting the API state clears it so the test run exits promptly.
